rulesNotes: 45 general education + 42 Professional Business Requirements + 18 Accounting + 15 free electives = 120 semester credits.

12 upper-level area-of-study credits, the upper-level capstone, and one additional three-credit upper-level course in the area of study or Professional Business Requirements. Both required Accounting courses are lower level; all four selected additional Accounting courses are upper level. The remaining six upper credits must therefore be in the business core, including the capstone.
The two required Accounting courses and four additional Accounting selections are allocated once. The fifth additional Accounting option, ACC-4110, is not an additional mandatory course.
This is the 18-credit Accounting area of study, not the separate 24-credit Accounting/CPA degree. No state CPA eligibility determination is made.
The general-education featured-course ledger retains HIS-1140 and PHI-1300 as the two allowed selected Human Cultures courses. No personal waiver is assumed.
The current catalog edition label was not exposed in the retrieved pages; the reviewed current-catalog identity is separate from dated tuition and provider evidence.
Standard residency and the combined alternative-source cap are separate. The 105 outside-credit bound is not a claim that 105 source-linked outside credits are available.
Source recommendation quantities, receiving-school quantities and personal approvals remain separate. Existing provider evidence retains its original dates and conditions.
At least half of the Accounting area of study must be current within ten years of the most recent application date; the business capstone has a five-year currency limit.
unresolved: Individual catalog eligibility, state CPA eligibility, course currency and registration availability depend on the student; this plan does not make a licensure or admissions decision.
Existing receiving-school transfer candidates retain their original provider/version/format restrictions. No additional provider award is inferred from a matching course title.
The standard nonmilitary residency route is modeled. Military enrollment, foreign-credit rules and Edison Accelerate require a separately evaluated scenario.
Published tuition is a planning basis; books, provider subscriptions and applicable fees are separate.
